decisions.reason: An encrypted second channel for messages is the firm's core trusted-communication competence, so it builds directly on its cryptography and authentication knowledge.
Mobile PDF signing fits the firm's stated move toward online contract signing and draws on its signature and cryptography know-how, though signing services are a more competitive adjacent field.
A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture describes the firm's integrated platform itself, so it is deeply embedded in existing R&D and unlikely to be withdrawn.
Email-to-app secure delivery extends the firm's secure-messaging capability, but it is a niche add-on whose early uptake is harder to read, which makes it somewhat more vulnerable.
A QR-code hardware token draws on the firm's hardware and transaction-signing experience in banking, but hardware tokens face pressure from app-based authentication.

A payment-network compliance suite is further from the firm's core identity and crypto knowledge and more consultancy-like, so it faces the highest risk, though compliance demand from banking customers likely keeps it on the market.
